160373.title: Spreadsheet: Vector column auto fit width issue when component values differ greatly
160373.feasibility_reason: The issue clearly identifies the problem in the spreadsheet column width calculation for vector/multi-component types where total width is divided equally instead of per-component sizing, but locating the exact UI layout code for the spreadsheet columns requires navigating Blender's UI/editors codebase.
160373.problem_summary: Auto-fitting column width in the Spreadsheet editor truncates wide vector components when component values differ significantly because width estimation computes the concatenated string width rather than accounting for the equal-width division among vector components.
160373.root_cause_hypothesis: The column width estimation function (likely `estimate_max_column_width` or component value formatters in `space_spreadsheet`) measures the width of the full formatted vector string as a single text block. However, the spreadsheet renderer allocates equal column sub-widths for each component, causing components wider than the average component width to be clipped.
160373.suggested_approach: Adjust the column width estimation logic for multi-component types (such as vectors, colors, and quaternions) so that the estimated cell width is based on the maximum width required by any individual component multiplied by the number of components (accounting for inter-component padding and separators).
prerequisites: A working Blender C++ development and build environment
Familiarity with the Spreadsheet editor codebase (`space_spreadsheet`) and UI font/string width calculation utilities
implementation_steps: Locate the column width auto-fit and width estimation implementation, specifically `estimate_max_column_width` or similar functions in `source/blender/editors/space_spreadsheet/`.
Inspect how multi-component data types (e.g., float2/3/4, int2/3, color, quaternion) are formatted and measured during column width auto-fitting.
Update the measurement logic for multi-component types to evaluate the string representation or pixel width of each component individually for sample rows.
Calculate the cell width requirement as `(max_component_width * num_components) + component_separators_padding`, ensuring the longest component fits within its allocated sub-cell slot.
Verify font metrics measurement handling (e.g., using `BLF_width` or estimated character length consistent with the rest of the spreadsheet auto-fit logic).

Test with the reproduction file containing vector values with extreme differences in magnitude (e.g., `1000000000, 0, 0`) and confirm auto-fit allocates sufficient width without clipping any component.
Verify regression behavior on single-value columns (float, int, string, boolean) and other vector/color columns.

153791.title: Sculpt: Add ability to toggle X, Y, Z radial symmetry independent of count
153791.feasibility_reason: The issue provides a clear task list for adding a toggle for radial symmetry independent of the count, but it touches multiple subsystems (UI, Paint struct data, and sculpting/painting logic) in a complex C/C++ codebase like Blender.
153791.problem_summary: Radial symmetry in Sculpt mode currently relies solely on a count per axis (where 1 means disabled), preventing users from toggling radial symmetry on/off independently of their chosen segment count or assigning hotkeys to toggle it.
153791.root_cause_hypothesis: The radial symmetry state is stored exclusively as segment counts in DNA (`Paint.radial_sym[3]`), conflating the enabled state with the segment count value. Consequently, disabling symmetry resets or overwrites the count, and no discrete boolean toggle exists in RNA or UI.
153791.suggested_approach: Introduce a bitmask flag in DNA (such as in `Paint` symmetry flags) for enabling radial symmetry on X, Y, and Z axes. Expose these toggles via RNA, update the sculpt/paint UI to show checkboxes alongside the count spinners, update sculpt execution code to check both the toggle flag and segment count, and add necessary do_versions logic.
prerequisites: A working Blender build environment from source (C/C++ and Python)
Understanding of Blender's DNA/RNA architecture and versioning system
Familiarity with sculpt and paint symmetry handling in Blender
implementation_steps: Define new flag bits in `DNA_brush_types.h` (e.g., `PAINT_RADIAL_SYM_X`, `PAINT_RADIAL_SYM_Y`, `PAINT_RADIAL_SYM_Z`) in `ePaintSymmetryFlags` or a new radial symmetry bitfield in the `Paint` struct.

Expose RNA boolean properties (e.g., `use_radial_symmetry_x`, `use_radial_symmetry_y`, `use_radial_symmetry_z` or a composite enum/flag `use_radial_symmetry`) on `Paint` / `Sculpt` in `source/blender/makesrna/intern/rna_sculpt_paint.c`.

Add versioning code in `source/blender/blenloader/intern/versioning_*.cc` to initialize the radial symmetry flags to true for axes where existing files have `radial_sym[i] > 1` (or maintain backward compatibility).

Update sculpt and paint symmetry iteration logic (e.g., in `sculpt.cc` / `sculpt_intern.hh` where radial symmetry passes are looped) to verify the axis flag is active before iterating beyond 1 repetition.

Update the Sculpt UI in Python (`properties_paint_common.py` or the symmetry popover in 3D Viewport header) to display toggle checkboxes for X, Y, Z next to their respective segment count inputs, disabling or muting the count input when the toggle is off.
Test sculpting with radial symmetry enabled, toggled off, and toggled back on, verifying that the configured segment count is preserved and keybindings can be assigned to the new RNA properties.

164257.title: Console: Mouse text selection does not continue through scrollback while dragging
164257.feasibility_reason: The issue describes a missing UI interaction feature (auto-scrolling during text selection drag) in Blender's Python Console. While the reproduction steps are clear, implementing continuous mouse drag selection with auto-scrolling requires deep knowledge of Blender's event handling, window manager, and the specific UI drawing/scrolling loop of the console region.
blockers: Requires familiarity with Blender's custom UI event handling and console scrolling mechanisms.
164257.problem_summary: In the Blender Python Console, selecting text via mouse drag does not auto-scroll the viewport when reaching the upper or lower boundaries of the view, preventing continuous selection of output spanning across multiple screens.
164257.root_cause_hypothesis: The console mouse selection operator (`CONSOLE_OT_select_set` / selection modal handling in `console_ops.cc`) only calculates selection coordinates within the currently visible viewport during mouse move events. It lacks a timer or modal auto-scroll handler to continuously increment/decrement the console scroll offset when the mouse cursor is held beyond the vertical region boundaries, and selection coordinates may not properly account for or update with view scroll offsets across frames.
164257.suggested_approach: Implement auto-scrolling during modal selection in the Console editor (similar to how text editor or outliner selection dragging operates). Register a modal timer while mouse dragging for selection; when the cursor is held near or outside the top/bottom boundaries of the console region, incrementally scroll the console view (`sc->scroll`) and re-evaluate the text selection endpoint based on the updated scroll offset.
prerequisites: Working Blender build environment (C/C++ toolchain, CMake)
Familiarity with Blender's window manager modal operator lifecycle (modal timer, WM_event_add_timer, WM_event_remove_timer)
Understanding of `SpaceConsole` struct, console line data structures, and scroll offset handling
implementation_steps: Locate the text selection operator in `source/blender/editors/space_console/console_ops.cc` (e.g., `console_select_set_invoke` / `console_select_set_modal` or equivalent operator).

Check how the Text Editor (`source/blender/editors/space_text/text_ops.cc`) handles drag-selection and auto-scroll (e.g., setting a timer with `WM_event_add_timer` on modal drag start and removing it on modal release/cancel).
Extend the console selection modal operator to register a window manager timer (`TIMER` event) while the mouse button is pressed and dragged.
In the modal event handler, on `TIMER` events, check if the mouse cursor coordinates are above the top or below the bottom edge of `ARegion`.
If outside the bounds, adjust the console view scroll offset (`sc->scroll`) by a speed factor proportional to the distance from the region edge, clamping within valid scroll limits.
Update the console selection endpoint using the updated mouse position mapped into the newly scrolled console text lines.
Tag the region for redraw (`ED_region_tag_redraw(region)`) so that both the scroll change and the extended selection highlight are immediately visible.
Clean up the timer upon mouse release (`LEFTMOUSE` release) or modal cancel (`ESC`).
Test text selection across multi-page console output by dragging above and below the visible region, ensuring smooth scrolling and correct buffer copy behavior (Ctrl+C / Cmd+C).

136889.title: Scale Cage in ortho view scales other axis unintuitively
136889.feasibility_reason: The issue describes an unintuitive scaling behavior specific to the cage scale tool in orthographic views. While steps to reproduce are clear, figuring out the orthographic projection math vs. screen-space interaction for gizmos can be subtle without prior familiarity with the gizmo/transform system.
136889.problem_summary: When using the Scale Cage tool in an aligned orthographic view, dragging what visually appears to be a side handle unexpectedly scales the object along two axes instead of just the active view axis.
136889.root_cause_hypothesis: The 3D cage gizmo distinguishes between corner handles (3 axes), edge handles (2 axes), and face handles (1 axis). In an aligned orthographic view (e.g., Front view), the silhouette handles on the sides correspond to the cage's 3D edges (which scale along both the screen axis and depth axis), while the 1-axis face center handle is positioned directly in the center facing the camera or obscured. Users clicking the side handle expect a 1D scale along the visible screen axis.
136889.suggested_approach: Detect when the 3D cage gizmo is used in an aligned orthographic view (or when an edge handle is parallel to the view direction), and either project/constrain edge handle transformations to only affect the orthogonal screen axis (ignoring the depth axis), or adapt the gizmo handle hit-testing/display in orthographic projection so that side interactions behave as 1D face handles.
prerequisites: Ability to build Blender from source
Basic familiarity with Blender's gizmo architecture and orthographic view transform matrix math
implementation_steps: Locate the 3D cage gizmo implementation (typically under `source/blender/editors/gizmo_library/gizmo_types/cage3d_gizmo.cc` or `transform_gizmo_cage.cc`).
Analyze how cage handles are represented, selected, and mapped to scale transform axes during drag operations (distinguishing face, edge, and corner interactions).

Inspect the transform handler when dragging edge handles; determine how the view projection matrix or camera orientation can be queried (e.g., checking if the view is orthographic and aligned with a principal axis).

Implement logic in the cage drag operator / gizmo interaction callback to suppress or lock the depth axis when dragging an edge handle that lies parallel to the view direction in orthographic projection.
Verify whether gizmo drawing/highlighting in orthographic view needs adjustments to avoid visual confusion over which axis is being influenced.

Test behavior in Perspective view (verify standard 3-axis/2-axis/1-axis cage scaling is preserved) and in Top, Front, Right orthographic views (verify side handles only scale the expected screen axis).
